transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-05
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Rafael (Redwood SE), Aisha (Stormforge), Devon (Stormforge), Elena (Stormforge)

Auto-summary:
Brief: Kickoff to scope POC acceptance criteria for Stormforge's assistant/summary product. Focus areas: measurable success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan (golden prompts + regression set), hallucination and format checks, and a 6-week timeline with deliverables.

Topics:
- Success criteria (latency, throughput, quality thresholds)
- Workload characteristics and sizing (tokens, concurrency)
- Benchmark plan: golden prompts, regression corpus, scoring approach
- Data handling/security constraints and deployment model discussion
- Timeline & next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros — i'm maya, i'll be your account lead. rafael's our se who will lead the benchmark work.
[00:12] Aisha (Stormforge): thanks, hi i'm aisha — head of ml at stormforge, excited to see how this POC will map to our production needs.
[00:18] Devon (Stormforge): devon here, platform lead, i'll own infra and sizing questions.
[00:23] Rafael (Redwood): nice to meet you all. quick agenda: align on acceptance criteria, agree workload shape, define golden prompts & regression tests, and land on a 4-6 week runbook. Does that work?
[00:32] Elena (Stormforge): yes that sounds good.
[00:35] Maya (Redwood): great, so to start — aisha can you describe success metrics from your side? what does a successful POC look like?
[00:42] Aisha (Stormforge): sure. three pillars: first, latency — 95th percentile under ~250ms for our short-form queries, second, throughput — support sustained 80 rps in peak windows, third, quality — hallucination rate below 2% and extraction F1 > 0.82 on our NER tasks. also reliability and reproducibility matter, we want deterministic rollbacks if quality regresses.
[01:05] Rafael (Redwood): good, that's concrete — we typically map those to an acceptance rubric: latency SLO, throughput target, and a quality score that's a weighted combo of automated metrics and human raters. for hallucination we recommend both automated detectors and spot human review on a golden set.
[01:22] Devon (Stormforge): quick Q on tokens — our average request is about 300 tokens, some long-form flows go to 2k tokens. daily volume is roughly 2 million tokens currently, peak concurrency 40 rps. does that change model choice?
[01:38] Rafael (Redwood): that pushes the need for models that handle KV cache efficiently and are quantized — sorry, that sounded like k-v cash in my notes — but yes, we want models and runtime optimizations for long-context. Also batching and prefix caching will affect cost and latency tradeoffs.
[01:55] Maya (Redwood): noted. For the POC we usually run two tracks: a quality track with a golden prompt + regression corpus, and a performance track with synthetic load replay to model your concurrency and token distribution.
[02:08] Aisha (Stormforge): can you talk about golden prompts — what do you expect from us vs what you'll provide?
[02:13] Rafael (Redwood): we'll supply a golden prompt template and some examples (structured system + user instructions, expected format). you should provide representative intents and edge-case queries — the golden set is typically 200-500 items that cover high-value flows, plus a larger regression corpus (2-5k) for automated checks.
[02:30] Elena (Stormforge): do you also generate variations for paraphrase robustness?
[02:33] Rafael (Redwood): yes we recommend paraphrase variants and adversarial cases. we run both exact-match structural tests (format validation) and semantic scoring.
[02:40] Maya (Redwood): on scoring approach: we propose a three-tier score:
- automated metric layer: BLEU/ROUGE or embedding-similarity for free-text, plus structured-field exact matches
- hallucination detector flags (heuristic + confidence thresholds)
- human rater validation on a stratified sample
we then aggregate into a composite quality score with weights you pick (e.g., 60% automated + 40% human).
[03:05] Aisha (Stormforge): that seems reasonable. for our NER entity extraction we want F1 to be the primary metric and hallucination penalties applied when hallucination causes false positives that impact auto-routing.
[03:18] Rafael (Redwood): understood. we'll build a custom scoring script so it's reproducible — you'll be able to run it locally or we can run it in our private deployment.
[03:26] Devon (Stormforge): on the infra sizing/hosted vs dedicated question — how do you recommend we proceed during POC? we have compliance pressures, but we can start hosted for speed.
[03:36] Maya (Redwood): typical flow: start hosted to iterate quickly on prompts and scoring. once the golden set and workloads are stable, we run a sizing call to estimate Dedicated pools or Private VPC. for compliance, we can run an initial security Q&A in parallel.
[03:48] Aisha (Stormforge): timeline? we were thinking a 6-week pilot. is that workable?
[03:52] Rafael (Redwood): yes — draft timeline we discussed aligns to 6 weeks:
- Week 0 (this week): align on success criteria & collect sample data
- Week 1: Redwood provides golden prompt template + initial baseline run on hosted with a small sample
- Week 2: prompt tuning + build regression corpus (2-5k) and create paraphrases
- Week 3: run full quality benchmarks and start manual review sampling
- Week 4: performance load tests, concurrency & token-budget validation (synthetic replay)
- Week 5: finalize RBAC/security checks, iterate on rules and fallback policies
- Week 6: deliver results, recommendations (model variant, quantization profile, routing policy) and acceptance decision
[04:23] Elena (Stormforge): what counts as an acceptable hallucination test? can you give examples of format checks?
[04:28] Rafael (Redwood): format checks: ensure JSON schema adherence, required fields present, field types correct. e.g., when we expect {"intent": "x", "entities": [{...}]}, any deviation is a fail. hallucination checks: we flag additions (entities not in source) and invented facts. we'll include two levels: automated heuristics (entity not in source, low confidence) and human adjudication.
[04:50] Aisha (Stormforge): for human raters, do you provide guidelines? we want consistent labeling across reviewers.
[04:55] Maya (Redwood): yes, we'll supply a rater guide with examples of true positives, false positives, hallucinations, and borderline cases. we'll also do a calibration session with your SMEs.
[05:04] Devon (Stormforge): what's the pass/fail logic? do you require all metrics to meet thresholds or a weighted composite?
[05:09] Rafael (Redwood): we recommend a weighted composite to avoid brittle pass/fail. e.g., 30% latency, 30% throughput/cost, 40% quality. you can set hard gates for critical items (e.g., hallucination must be <2%).
[05:22] Aisha (Stormforge): cost sensitivity — if a model meets quality but costs 3x our target, we won't accept it. can you include cost modeling in the benchmark?
[05:31] Maya (Redwood): absolutely. Redwood Optimize will output per-token cost estimates and recommend quantization or alternative model variants. we'll surface cost vs quality tradeoffs in the final report.
[05:41] Elena (Stormforge): curious about regression tests. do you keep a holdout set? how often do you run regression?
[05:46] Rafael (Redwood): yes — we create a golden set (human reviewed) and a larger regression holdout. we run regression every time we change prompts or models; for the POC we run nightly regression for the week of performance tests, and a full sweep before the acceptance review. post-POC we recommend a gating pipeline for model rollouts.
[06:03] Aisha (Stormforge): ok. on data — we need to anonymize personally identifiable info. are there tools you use to scrub PII before benchmarks?
[06:10] Rafael (Redwood): we have scripts and patterns for common PII; we can share a scrubbing checklist. if anything is sensitive, you can provide an anonymized sample or run benchmarks in your private deployment.
[06:18] Maya (Redwood): action items recap, we'll put this in the notes, but quick recap now: maya to share spreadsheet + golden prompt template; rafael to run hosted baseline and share logs; aisha to send sample dataset; devon to confirm concurrency & token budget.
[06:31] Devon (Stormforge): ok i'll confirm and share by next thursday.
[06:34] Aisha (Stormforge): we'll aim to have the 5k anonymized records by friday.
[06:38] Rafael (Redwood): one note on metrics: for embedding/similarity checks we recommend cosine thresholding and a manual review on borderline cases. also for hallucination scoring we'll use precision-weighted penalties so a single hallucination in a big doc doesn't doom the whole item.
[06:53] Maya (Redwood): excellent. anything else on security or compliance?
[06:57] Elena (Stormforge): our security team will ping the SOC2 questionnaire to your security contact; we may request a private deployment if the questionnaire flags anything.
[07:05] Maya (Redwood): understood — we'll get that started in parallel.
[07:08] Aisha (Stormforge): final question — do you recommend any tooling for continuous regression once we move to production?
[07:13] Rafael (Redwood): Redwood Optimize plus our tracing and alerting — you can connect token-level costs and per-prompt regression alerts. we'll propose thresholds and automatic rollback policies.
[07:24] Maya (Redwood): ok let's close with timeline and concrete deliverables. we'll circulate the spreadsheet today and aim to have baseline runs next week.
[07:31] Devon (Stormforge): sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:34] Maya (Redwood): thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the infra sizing + security sync.

End of transcript.

Notes on imperfect transcription: several acronyms mis-captured (KV cache -> k-v cash), occasional filler words and overlap. Some product names transcribed generically (Redwood Optimize referred to as "optimize tool" intermittently).

Quick checklist (to be included with the spreadsheet):
- Golden set: 200-500 human-reviewed prompts covering high-value flows
- Regression corpus: 2-5k Examples including paraphrases and adversarials
- Automated checks: schema validation, entity precision/recall, embedding-similarity thresholds
- Hallucination checks: automated detectors + 5-10% human sample for adjudication
- Performance tests: synthetic replay with same token distribution, target peak of 80 rps, targets for 95p latency <250ms
- Cost model: per-token cost and recommendations for quantization/alternate variants

Deliverables from Redwood by 2027-09-07: benchmark spreadsheet, golden prompt template, scrubbing checklist, rater guide.

Deliverables from Stormforge by 2027-09-09: anonymized sample dataset (5k rows), concurrency confirmations, list of critical intents.

Meeting closed at ~16:45 UTC.
